sources.entry: Huginn - Build agents that monitor and act on your behalf. MIT Ruby
Huginn | Build agents that monitor the web and act on your behalf

summary.one_liner: Huginn is a self-hosted system for building agents that monitor the web and other sources, then take actions on your behalf, like a hackable IFTTT or Zapier on your own server.
summary.what_it_does: Agents create and consume events, passing them along a directed graph. The README lists uses such as scraping websites and emailing on change, watching RSS feeds, IMAP mailboxes, webhooks and MQTT topics, and tracking weather or travel deals. Agents can post to Slack, Telegram, Pushover, Twilio and other services, and call OpenAI-compatible APIs to summarize, classify, translate, or generate images and speech. They can store files on Dropbox, S3, FTP and the local filesystem, run custom logic in JavaScript, Liquid or jq, and publish feeds or JSON endpoints from collected events. Additional Agents can be added as external gems.
use_cases: Get an email when a web page changes
Monitor RSS feeds or IMAP mailboxes and forward matching items
Receive weather alerts such as rain forecasts
Post automated updates to Slack, Telegram or other chat services
how_to_run: Open the web UI and log in as admin with the password printed in the container log
For local development: cp .env.example .env, then bundle and npm install
bundle exec rake db:create && bundle exec rake db:migrate && bundle exec rake db:seed
notable: Agents are chained in a directed event graph, similar to IFTTT or Zapier but self-hosted
Custom logic via JavaScript, Liquid templates or jq
Extensible through external Agent gems loaded with ADDITIONAL_GEMS
Official Docker images, including a single-process variant for separate worker containers
Can publish feeds and JSON endpoints from collected events
caveats: A background worker must stay running, so hosting needs an always-on process and usually a managed database; no free-tier worker on the listed platforms
Running the full spec suite needs Chrome and ChromeDriver or the Docker test environment
Community packages on YunoHost and Unraid may lag behind releases
keywords: share automation on my own server
